subject: Criteria runway and evidence catalog for MAP & acceptance tests
messages:
From: Laura Schmidt <laura@clearcare.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — MAP and acceptance tests

Thanks for the walkthrough today — the team found the latency profile and the model explainability hooks compelling. Before we commit to a pilot I need a concrete mutual action plan with: 1) explicit acceptance tests and examples of evidence we would provide/expect, 2) owners for each test, and 3) a realistic runway to close so our procurement and security teams can line up.

High level asks from ClearCare:
- Pilot go/no-go by end of October (but we can be flexible by 1–2 weeks).
- Evidence we can hand to our compliance team (logs, retention policy, SOC2 pointer).
- Clear acceptance tests for: latency, throughput, inference accuracy on a holdout slice, and false positive rate for triage rules.

Could you share a catalog of the acceptance tests and a proposal for who on your side owns each one? Also include an example of the raw artifacts we should collect during smoke and full-run tests.

Thanks — happy to hop on 30m if helpful.

—Laura
Laura Schmidt
Director, Product Operations
ClearCare Health

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Laura Schmidt <laura@clearcare.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T12:42:00-07:00
Subject: Criteria runway and evidence catalog for MAP & acceptance tests

Laura — thanks for the clear asks and for joining today. Attached are two artifacts to start: MAP_v2.xlsx (a working MAP with milestones) and acceptance-evidence-samples.pdf (examples of logs, traces, and evaluation reports). Summary of the proposed approach (short runway, staged verification so you can unblock procurement while we run quality checks):

1) Runway & staging (owner in parentheses)
- Stage 0: Kickoff + infra checklist (Redwood: jonas_weber) — infra health, VPC, KMS, access controls. Deliverable: infra health report and shared test endpoints. Target: Day 0–3 after SOW.
- Stage 1: Smoke & safety (Redwood: marissa_cole / ClearCare: Laura) — basic correctness on 200 sample prompts, safety filters engaged, Latency SLO sanity check. Acceptance: 90th %tile latency < 350ms for standard requests, no high-severity safety flags on sample set. Deliverable: smoke-report.json, sample transcripts. Target: Day 3–7.
- Stage 2: Quality & concordance (Redwood: olga_petrov / ClearCare: Product Eng lead) — run a labeled holdout against model variants. Acceptance: task-specific metric (we propose F1 >= 0.86 on the holdout OR top-1 accuracy >= 92% for classification tasks). Deliverable: evaluation-runbook.csv, confusion matrix, error-case index. Target: Day 8–18.
- Stage 3: Load & resiliency (Redwood: ben_carter / ClearCare: SRE) — throughput and failover tests with productionish traffic. Acceptance: 99.9% availability during the run; graceful degradation plan validated. Deliverable: load-test-report.html, perf-traces.zip. Target: Day 19–24.
- Stage 4: Canary cut + business signoff (joint) — canary at 5–10% traffic, monitor for regressions for 72h. Acceptance: no regression in key metrics and stakeholder signoff. Deliverable: canary dashboard snapshot, decision memo. Target: Day 25–30.

2) Acceptance test examples (what we will collect)
- Latency SLOs: raw token timing traces, p95/p99 tables, distribution plots (CSV/PNG).
- Quality: labeled predictions vs. ground truth, scripts to reproduce the eval, diff reports between model versions.
- Safety/Policy: policy hits logs with redaction, examples of filtered outputs and rationale.
- Observability: per-request trace id, sampling of full transcripts, and aggregated cost/latency per route.

3) Decision matrix & stoplight (pass/fail)
- For each test we include threshold, measurement method, owner, and an evidence file link. Any single critical-safety failure is a hard stop; other failures route to remediation lanes with defined re-test cadence.

4) Quick ask from your side
- Confirm the ClearCare evaluation lead and an SRE contact who can own perf runs.
- Do you have a canonical holdout dataset or should we run with the sample set from today?

I attached the MAP_v2.xlsx with the milestone table and the evidence catalog draft. If you're ok I can lock owners and schedule the smoke run as early as Monday.

—Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx)

Forwarding with a couple of clarifications for owners and test artifacts — see below for the proposed short checklist I'll run in the smoke: 

--Checklist for Stage 1 smoke (owner: marissa_cole)
- Run 200 sample prompts through test endpoint (script: smoke_run.sh). Output: smoke-report.json (includes per-request latency, model-id used, policy flags).
- Generate a 20-item exception index (CSV) with categories: hallucination, truncation, latency spike, safety-hit.
- Provide a 5-minute trace export for 10 example requests.

I also added two quick examples to the acceptance-evidence-samples.pdf under section A (sample trace + redaction example). I'm OK to schedule the smoke on Monday morning — I'll coordinate with ben for perf toggles.

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@healthops.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Schmidt <laura@clearcare.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Criteria runway and evidence catalog for MAP & acceptance tests

Thanks — this structure looks good and I appreciate the explicit artifacts. A couple of small asks from our side before we lock the SOW: 
- Can we tighten Stage 1 latency p95 target to 300ms rather than 350ms for standard requests? Our user flows are latency-sensitive and procurement will flag anything above 300ms. If that's hard for all requests, we can make it a weighted target (core routes 300ms, non-core 350ms).
- For Stage 2 quality metrics, instead of a single F1 threshold can we use a pass/fail on a set of probes (at least 3 probe categories must meet thresholds) — I can share the probe list tomorrow.
- We want a short canary extension option: if any metric is within 2% of the threshold, allow a 7-day canary extension instead of an immediate rollback. Add that to the decision matrix as an explicit remediation path.

If you can update the MAP_v2.xlsx with those callouts I can push this through procurement quickly. Happy to review the attachment and join a 30m alignment on Friday if useful.

—Tom Reed
Head of Integrations, HealthOps (contracted on ClearCare pilot)
(attachment: proposed-probes.csv)
